title: Sweden under the gold standard: the consumer price index and the December values of the Riksbank's discount rate and of the yield on government bonds, annual, 1870-1913
source: Sveriges riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden: Volume I, ch. 8 (R. Edvinsson and J. Soederberg, 'The evolution of Swedish consumer prices, 1290-2008', 2010), Table I.A8.1 'A Consumer Price Index for Sweden 1290-' (file volym1/volumeich8consumerpriceindex.xls, version 2.1); Volume II, ch. 6 (D. Waldenstroem, 'Swedish stock and bond returns, 1856-2012', 2014), Tables II.A6.3, II.A6.9 and II.A6.10 (file volym2/volumeiich6stocksandbonds.xls, version 2.0)
series: year; cpi_1914_100: Table I.A8.1, 'Deflation index 1914 = 100' (the printed table says July 1914 = 100; for 1732-1914 the index rests on Joerberg 1972 and Myrdal 1933, with its own weights for 1870-1913); discount_rate_dec and bond_yield_dec: Table II.A6.3 'Yields on short- and long-term government securities, 1856-', columns 'Short-term government bill yield' (the Riksbank's discount rate before 1983) and 'Long-term government bond yield' (from 1874), per cent; the fetch script checks that they are the December values of Tables II.A6.9 and II.A6.10
license: Sveriges riksbank's terms for its open data: 'The Riksbank's open data is freely available and may be further used without any special consent or agreement being required. Enter source, Sveriges riksbank and date. If you have processed statistics taken from the Riksbank's website, you may not state Sveriges Riksbank as the source.' The snapshot stores the values as published (source: Sveriges riksbank, 2026-10-16). The averages, changes and correlations the chapter computes from them are the book's own calculations and are attributed to the book and to Edvinsson and Soederberg (2010) and Waldenstroem (2014), not to the Riksbank.
notes: The krona replaced the riksdaler in 1873 with the gold standard (1 krona = 0.403225 grams of gold; wicksell_facts rows rk_title, rk_gram). The chapter uses 1874-1913, the years with both rates; the annual rates it uses are the means of the twelve monthly values (snapshot riksbank_sweden_monthly_1870_1913). Edvinsson and Soederberg's printed Table A8.1 has the same values for 1887 and 1913 (wicksell_facts rows es_1887, es_1913).
citation: Edvinsson, R. and J. Soederberg (2010), 'The evolution of Swedish consumer prices, 1290-2008', and Waldenstroem, D. (2014), 'Swedish stock and bond returns, 1856-2012', in R. Edvinsson, T. Jacobson and D. Waldenstroem (eds.), Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volumes I and II, Stockholm: Ekerlids forlag and Sveriges Riksbank
